notes: I kept the nano1 3V3 connection and did not change the graph, because the E8 warning is not a real problem for this manual. The catalogue's 4.5-21 V supply range is for powering the board in. This tutorial powers both boards over USB (5 V), which is within range. The 3V3 pin is the board's 3.3 V regulated output, so it is not a power input and does not need 4.5 V. The circuit image labels the pin '3V' and uses it only as the pull-up voltage for SDA and SCL. Moving the pull-ups to 5 V or VUSB would be the real error here, because the Nano 33 IoT's I/O pins are 3.3 V only and not 5 V tolerant.

Step 1 listed 10 jumper wires, including wire9 and wire10 as spares. I dropped them in step 2 because neither the circuit image nor the text gives them any connection. The 8 wires kept are the ones the circuit needs. The parts list of 10 is a pack size.

The image shows no breadboards. I assumed the two mini breadboards from the parts list: bb1 on the reader side holds both 4.7 kΩ pull-ups and the 3V3 rail, and bb2 on the writer side is a junction. wire7 and wire8 carry SCL and SDA between them. Exact hole positions are my choice.

SCL is on A5 and SDA is on A4 of both boards, as the tutorial says. Each line has one 4.7 kΩ pull-up resistor to the 3V3 rail on bb1, which the reader's 3V3 pin feeds. The image shows the same layout.
GND is a single direct wire between the two boards' GND pins (the image shows it that way).
In the catalogue every 'tp' hole is one strip, so tp.1, tp.2 and tp.3 are the same node.
Each board is powered by its own USB cable from the computer. The computer is not a graph node, so each USB cable connects only to its board's USB port.
